study_identification_part.si4_title: Multiscale heterogeneity of functional connectivity in autism

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objectives: to use normative modelling to examine heterogeneity of functional connectivity (FC) in autism at multiple scales (connections, regions, networks) and to assess relations with clinical measures. This satisfies all criteria: explicit research questions and explicit purpose of applying normative modeling (to characterize heterogeneity and relate deviation patterns to clinical variables).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Here, we used normative modelling to examine FC heterogeneity at the level of pair-wise inter-regional connections, specific brain regions, and broader functional networks... FC deviation patterns across coarser levels correlated with social functioning symptoms and intellectual ability."; "We applied a multiscale normative modeling approach to characterize and compare the inter-individual heterogeneity of FC in autism at three levels... We then assessed the predictive accuracy of extreme deviations... in relation to clinical measures..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This is a NEW normative model trained on neurotypical controls pooled from LEAP and ABIDE. The study reports the final sample sizes and indicates that quality control and exclusion criteria are used, but defers details to the Supplement. Eligibility criteria for the reference cohort and explicit image quality standards are not fully described in the main text; reasons for exclusion are not listed here.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Quality control and exclusion criteria are detailed in the Supplement Section 2 and follow previous work (Ilioska et al., 2023)."; "The final sample included 796 autistic individuals... and 1028 neuro-typical (NT) individuals... recruited across 32 different sites."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age, sex, and head motion (mean framewise displacement) are included as covariates in the normative model. Multi-site effects are addressed by ComBat harmonization to regress site-specific effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "We used gaussian process regression... using age, sex, and mean framewise displacement."; "We used ComBat... to regress the scan-site-specific effects from the FC data."
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: Ilioska2024.pdf.md — Normative modeling; Mapping functional connectivity

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We pooled scans from three large datasets: the EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP)... and the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchanges I and II, or ABIDE-I and ABIDE-II..."
